record.title: Microduck trunk base plate — the 'trunk_base' body mesh of Pollen's MJCF: 57 x 36 x 1 mm chassis plate with two Ø19 hip-yaw holes 35 mm apart, 4 x Ø2.3 M2 clearance holes, a 6 x 12 cable slot and four Ø1.8 locating pins
record.why: cad/part.py builds one valid solid (bin/cad part:microduck-trunk-base, 2026-09-01) and ce-cad/bin/cad-refcheck grades it against Pollen's own published mesh reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/trunk_base.stl: p95 surface distance 0.001 mm both ways (max 0.009), bbox delta 0.00 mm on every axis, 6/6 holes matched (2 x Ø19.0, 4 x Ø2.3). Round 1 PASS; the report is the ledger artifact.
record.origin_why: modelled by hand in cecad from measurements taken off Pollen Robotics' decimated visual mesh (CC BY-SA-NC sim asset) with cad-mjcf sections/probe and cecad.meshfeatures; nobody has Pollen's CAD and no physical part has been measured. Admitted through the TRIAD.md door: evidence/ledger.jsonl + computed trust.json.
record.source_reference: reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/trunk_base.stl (Onshape doc 804927696f06d877f3f1803e, exported by onshape-to-robot); placed in body trunk_base at pos (4, 0, -17.5) mm, quat wxyz (0.707, 0, 0, 0.707) per spec/mesh-placements.json
record.why_this_folder_exists: The chassis plate both hip-yaw XL330s hang from and the power_support bolts to; every leg load passes through it. Nothing on the shelf is a 57 x 36 plate with two Ø19 servo-hub holes on a 35 mm pitch.
